keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The Rewa State page gives 33,670 km2 for 1901 and no area or boundary for any earlier date: it has only the founding at Bandhavgarh 'in 1140 CE' ('according to legend'), the fort as the Baghela capital 'until its destruction in 1597 by Akbar' and the move to Rewa in 1617. fx-37 (handoff H50 from fx-32): for 1140-1616 a 60 km disc about the fort (11,300 km2, about 45 cells) replaces the 1901 outline, which sat on Rewa city and on 80-88 cells of Cliopatria's Chandela outlines of 1085-1314. The Chandelas of Jejakabhukti page has the Chandelas only possibly annexing 'the northern part of the Baghelkhand region' under Madanavarman and losing it to the Kalachuri Narasimha (undated), and the Baghelas only as one of the 'local dynasties' that rose in the decline under Hammiravarman (r. c. 1288-1311); it names neither Rewa nor Bandhavgarh. The disc is soft (confidence 1). Review fx-37: the disc now ends in 1499, not 1616: the Rewa State page has 'Until the 15th century, the Baghela's of Bandhogarh were engaged in extending their possessions', Sikandar Lodi failing to take the Bandhogarh fort in 1498-1499, and Maharaja Veer Singh Deo (r. 1500-1540) who 'established the town of Birsinghpur' (Satna district, 24.48 N 80.58 E, 95 km from the fort, outside the disc and inside the 1901 outline); the 1901 outline is drawn from 1500 (rewa-state_1500). The disc still shares 17-18 cells with the Cliopatria Chandela Kingdom outlines of 1152-1305 (against 80-88 for the 1901 outline); the size rule leaves them to the smaller Rewa, which also removes the 124-cell overlap with the Tughlaq shapes of 1320-1351.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives 33,670 km2 for 1901 and no area or boundary for any other date; a hand-drawn outline of 33,900 km2 (ratio 1.0) about Rewa, from the Mirzapur border to Amarkantak, stands in for 1500-1799. Review fx-37: from 1500, not from the 1617 capital move ('In 1617, Maharaja Vikramaditya Singh Baghel moved his capital to Rewa'): the page has the Baghelas of Bandhogarh 'engaged in extending their possessions' until the 15th century and Veer Singh Deo (r. 1500-1540), who 'established the town of Birsinghpur' (Satna district, inside this outline, 95 km from Bandhavgarh); in 1580 Akbar merged the 'territory of Bandhogarh' into the Subah of Ilahabad. The early state at Bandhavgarh is rewa-state_1140. The Baghelkhand page gives 42,179 km2 for the whole region (undated). fx-37, handoff H50 from fx-32.

region.text: Bandhavgarh, the seat of the founding reign

ledger.note: About 1140: Raja Vyaghra Dev founds the Baghel kingdom at Bandhavgarh. "The ruler of Rewa ruled from Bandhavgarh during the founding reign of Raja Vyaghra Dev in 1140 CE" (infobox Established 1140, "legendary" in the article); the Baghelkhand page: "Rewa State was founded in the area circa 1140". The extent is a 40 km circle about the fort (my reading).

1617: the capital moves from Bandhavgarh to Rewa. "In 1617, Maharaja Vikramaditya Singh Baghel moved his capital to Rewa."; the rulers list says Vikramaditya Deo "founded the town of Rewa in 1618", so the year is 1617 or 1618 on the page. The Bandhavgarh Fort page is silent on the move.

ledger.note: Beginning of the 19th century: bridging, page silent on the year. The Rewa page: Sohagpur and Amarkantak were "seized by the Marathas" at "the beginning of the century"; it does not name Nagpur or the Bhonsle. Dated 1800 by reading; the extent is two 30 km circles.

region.text: the parganas of Sohagpur and Amarkantak

ledger.note: After the 1857 uprisings: bridging, page silent on the year. The parganas of Sohagpur and Amarkantak were "restored to his rule (having been seized by the Marathas" at the beginning of the century) after the uprisings of 1857; dated 1858 by reading, with the British as the restoring power (the page does not name them here). Raghuraj Singh became Maharaja in 1857.

ledger.note: 12 March 1948: Rewa merges into Vindhya Pradesh. "Vindhya Pradesh state was formed on 12 March 1948 and inaugurated on 4 April 1948" by the merger of 36 princely states, with Rewa, Panna, Datia, Orchha, Chhatarpur and Samthar named. The Rewa State page gives the accession to India in 1947 ("Upon India's independence in 1947, the maharaja of Rewa acceded unto the Dominion of India") and no merger year; its infobox ends in 1947. The Vindhya Pradesh page does not say that Rewa merged on the formation date; Vindhya Pradesh became Part C on 1 January 1950 and merged into Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 1956.

wars.name: Akbar at Bandhavgarh
wars.outcome: "Akbar intervened, captured and dismantled the Bandhavgarh Fort in 1597, after a war and siege of eight months."
wars.note: The page does not say how long the fort stayed in Mughal hands; the Bandhavgarh Fort page says only that it was under the Baghel kings of Rewa till 1947. Akbar was given refuge at Rewa at the age of 10 (undated) on the Rewa page.

certainty.note: The pages give an area for 1901 and no boundary; the shapes are a hand-drawn outline of that area and two circles.

sources.title: Rewa State
sources.note: Founded 1140 (legendary) at Bandhavgarh; Akbar captured Bandhavgarh in 1597; capital moved to Rewa in 1617 or 1618; British protectorate 5 October 1812; Sohagpur and Amarkantak seized by the Marathas and restored after 1857; direct British rule 1 April 1875 to 15 October 1895; accession 1947; area 33,670 km2 (1901).

sources.title: Vindhya Pradesh
sources.note: Formed 12 March 1948, inaugurated 4 April 1948, by the merger of 36 princely states including Rewa, Panna, Datia, Orchha, Chhatarpur and Samthar; Part C 1950; merged into Madhya Pradesh in 1956.

notes: Four pages opened (Rewa State, Vindhya Pradesh, Baghelkhand, Bandhavgarh Fort); Baghela dynasty returned url_not_found. The pages give no boundary and no area before 1901; the late state is drawn from 1140. Conflicts: capital to Rewa in 1617 (text) against 1618 (rulers list); infobox end 1947 (accession) against the merger into Vindhya Pradesh in 1948 (Vindhya page; the Rewa page gives no merger year); Vindhya Pradesh dissolved on 31 October 1956 against 1 November 1956 on the same page. The rulers list has a gap between 1630 and 1835. Not recorded: the British protectorate of 5 October 1812 after Pindari raids from Mirzapur territory (the british-empire dossier should record the vassal_start for rewa-state from 1812 to 1947, with the sub-period of direct administration 1 April 1875 to 15 October 1895 as an occupation or note). The page does not name Nagpur or the Bhonsle as the seizers of Sohagpur and Amarkantak; the kingdom-of-nagpur dossier has no matching gain, because none of the pages opened for it names Sohagpur or Amarkantak. Counterparts needing dossiers: vindhya-pradesh (1948-1956, post-independence union). Gazetteer lacks Rewa as a place; polygon and coordinates are used.
